title: Priority isolation and progressive shed strategy for GPU capacity exhaustion
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During the 2026-02-26 hosted capacity event a sustained tenant burst combined with autoscaler hysteresis caused multi-hour queue buildup and per-tenant unfair throttling. This ticket designs and delivers a short-term mitigations + medium-term system changes: 1) strict priority isolation so high-SLO tenants don't suffer starvation, 2) progressive (soft) shed policy that degrades noncritical traffic in stages instead of global hard drops, and 3) fast preemptive eviction for low-value work when a pool hits critical pressure. Goal: reduce P95 and P99 user-facing latencies during pool saturation and avoid long tail queue amplification while keeping unit cost low.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Captured findings from postmortem notes. Root causes: (a) autoscaler hysteresis delay, (b) admission scoring unaware of tenant SLO tiers, (c) heavy bursty KV-cache misses increasing per-request GPU time. Proposal: priority isolation + staged shed + admission shim. Filing as P0 because of repeated customer impact.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Liu: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Priority-Isolation-and-Progressive-Shed. Suggest starting with an admission-layer feature-flag and a per-pool credit ledger before deeper runtime changes. Want quick telemetry so rollbacks are fast.

2026-03-04 - Design review (Sanjay Rao): UX needs: Console indicators for pool pressure, per-tenant SLO tag, and an opt-out flag for dedicated customers. Also recommend an editor-friendly simulator to test shed schedules with real token distributions.

2026-03-05 - Infra review (Leah Kim): Autoscaler adjustments required: reduce scale-down hysteresis for bursty queues and surface a 'critical pressure' metric to the admission controller. Leah volunteered to add the metric to the exporter (PR linked below).

2026-03-07 - Marcus Liu: Implemented prototype admission shim and basic credit ledger. First smoke tests on staging showed CPU overhead ~1.8% and admission decision latency +1.2ms p50. Smoke test PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4392

2026-03-08 - Aisha Patel: Canary plan approved: enable progressive-shed on 5% of hosted capacity for one week. Metrics to watch: pool queue length, per-tenant P95/P99 latency, requests dropped per minute, and false-positive shed rate. Canary dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/canary/priority-shed-2026-03
2026-03-10 - Security (Omar Bashir): Confirmed no new data paths introduced; credit ledger stores opaque tenant IDs only. Security review not required but audit logging must be on for the canary.

2026-03-10 - Marcus Liu: Deployed canary. Early signals: noncritical tenants started to see increased 429s but high-SLO tenants stable. Observed one regression - a billing-service tenant incorrectly classified as noncritical; added test to mapping logic. Follow-up ticket ENG-215007 created for mapping fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Canary: progressive-shed enabled on 5% of hosted GPU pool traffic for 7 days with no customer-facing incidents (no drop in high-SLO tenant success rate).
Per-pool critical-pressure metric emitted and visible in Console within 1 hour of deployment.
Admission decision latency increase < 3ms p50 and < 8ms p99 at production traffic scales.
Automated unit and integration tests for credit ledger and mapping logic in CI.
action_items: ENG-215001: Implement per-pool credit ledger (owner: Marcus Liu, estimate: 3) - ledger enforces reserved credits for high-SLO tenants and applies soft-shed marks when credits exhausted.
ENG-215002: Add 'critical_pressure' metric and exporter label (owner: Leah Kim, estimate: 2) - used by autoscaler and admission shim. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2101
ENG-215003: Autoscaler hysteresis tuning (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 2) - reduce scale-down wait from 5m to 90s under burst mode and add immediate-prewarm signal on sustained queue growth.
ENG-215004: Admission shim feature-flag rollout & telemetry (owner: Marcus Liu, estimate: 2) - include console flags and canary target controls.
ENG-215005: Console UX: pool pressure indicator and tenant SLO tag editor (owner: Sanjay Rao, estimate: 3) - visible in per-model and per-route dashboards.
ENG-215006: Post-deploy regression tests and mapping validation (owner: QA Team, estimate: 2) - ensure billing and infra tenants are correctly classified.
ENG-215007: Fix tenant classification mapping bug discovered in canary (owner: Marcus Liu, estimate: 1) - verify via integration tests.
ENG-215008: Run load experiments to calibrate soft-shed thresholds across seq-length distributions (owner: Performance Team, estimate: 5) - produce benchmark artifact.
